text:
mia: FYI we've seen ~15% of audit events dropped during last spike (03:14 UTC). Need a quick sync on schema changes + customer-facing validation and how KMS affects throughput. :eyes:

jason: ouch. do we know which types are getting dropped? security vs telemetry?

mia: mostly resource.access and token.rotate events. smaller size but high QPS from a single tenant.

anika: could be backpressure at the ingest API layer. Are we returning 429s upstream or queuing and timing out?

sre-oncall: logs show the gateway returned 503 -> "ingest queue full" twice during the spike. Downstream Kafka handled it fine.

leo: is KMS in path sync for every event? I thought we used envelope encryption async in the pipeline.

mia: currently we sign+encrypt at API sync for tenant-level sensitive fields for PB data. That adds ~5-10ms/op CPU and spikes with many small events.

devops: long-term we should push encryption to a dedicated worker pool. short-term: can we batch-encrypt?

anika: batching makes sense but affects ordering for real-time alerts. propose: prioritization tiers - P0 (security) single-event sync, P1 (audit meta) batched with bounded delay (200ms), P2 (telemetry) best-effort.

jason: +1. Also we should expose a tenant config to opt into higher durability (sync encrypt) vs lower cost (async). customers asked for this.

mia: for customer-facing validation we need a strict JSON Schema so customers can reject invalid audit events server-side. Draft validator suggested below:

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["event_type","timestamp","tenant_id","actor"],
  "properties": {
    "event_type": {"type":"string"},
    "timestamp": {"type":"string","format":"date-time"},
    "tenant_id": {"type":"string"},
    "actor": {"type":"object"},
    "resource": {"type":"object"},
    "metadata": {"type":"object"}
  }
}
```

leo: nice. we should version the schema (v1, v2) and include schema_version in the envelope so customer validators can evolve.

sre-oncall: performance note: when we introduced schema validation at the gateway it added ~3ms per request under normal load, but during bursts it's a hotspot. Maybe move lightweight checks to gateway and full validation in async pipeline.

anika: agreed. gateway do presence + types. deeper rules in async worker. and provide an endpoint for customers to run their validators against our sample payloads.

jason: indexing/cost question: we store events in ES cluster today. high-cardinality fields explode costs. any proposals?

devops: options: roll up older events to compressed blob (cheap S3) and keep 30d in ES. or move to ClickHouse for cheaper ingestion and retention. both need reindexing work.

mia: cost constraint: one large tenant contributed 40% of audit tokens last month. need tenant-level throttles or separate billing tier.

leo: we can also reduce verboseness of events by moving large metadata into separate linked blobs. keep ES doc small with pointers.

anika: security/RBAC change: if we start exposing schema_version and event pointers, ensure RBAC disallows cross-tenant reference resolution. threat model: tenant A shouldn't be able to fetch tenant B blobs via pointer abuse.

jason: good catch. add tenant-scoped signed URLs and check KMS auth.

mia: vuln triage note: KMS client lib 2.1.3 flagged for CVE-2026-0421 (padding oracle) in our dependency scan. patching plan?

devops: upgrade to 2.1.5 fixes it. rolling patch deploy scheduled tonight for staging and tomorrow to prod if no regressions.

sre-oncall: add pre/post metrics for encryption latency so we can measure impact of 2.1.5.

anika: incident response playbook update: add an "audit-ingest degraded" runbook that includes toggling batching, enabling tenant throttles, and switching to degraded mode where we persist raw events to S3 for replay.

mia: love that. can someone draft the degraded playbook? assign, please.

jason: i'll draft the playbook sections for batching and throttles.

leo: i'll handle KMS upgrade validation and signed URL changes.

devops: i'll wire up the metric dashboards and add an alert for gateway queue depth > 80%.

anika: i'll own schema versioning and customer validator endpoint.

audit-ingest-bot: deploy job started: audit-ingest/patch-kms-2-1-5 -> staging (job id: deploy-8421).

mia: thanks. action items summarized:
- jason: draft degraded-mode playbook + throttle runbooks (ETA EOD)
- leo: KMS patch validation + signed URL RBAC changes (ETA +24h)
- devops: dashboards + alerts (ETA +12h)
- anika: schema versioning + customer validator endpoint spec (ETA +48h)
- mia: coordinate customer communication and temporary tenant throttles if needed

mia: marking this thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:

jason: thanks everyone. I'll post an initial PR for the playbook later today.

leo: reporting back in #eng-sre after staging verify.

sre-oncall: will monitor the queue alert and open incident if >90% for >5m.

mia: closing the thread once tickets exist.
